title: How to grow okra in containers
seoTitle: Growing Okra in Containers: Pot Size, Soil and Water
description: Yes, okra grows in containers. Use at least a 5-gallon pot with drainage holes, potting mix and full sun, and water often. What to expect from the harvest.
summary: Okra grows well in a container. Use at least a 5-gallon bucket with drainage holes, fill it with potting mix, give it full sun and water it often. Expect a shorter plant that starts producing later than okra in the ground.

targetQueries: can you grow okra in a pot
intro: No garden bed? Okra still works. A single plant in a 5-gallon bucket can keep you in pods through the summer, as long as it gets plenty of sun and water.
Need seeds? Start with [free okra seeds](/okra/free-okra-seeds) from Olivia's garden.

items: One plant per 5-gallon container or larger
At least 5 hours of direct sun, and 8 to 10 is better
Check the soil every day in summer

blocks.text: Olivia's grandfather grew Clemson Spineless from the project's seed in a 5-gallon bucket with drainage holes, filled with potting mix, about 15 miles from our garden in North Texas. He watered it every 2 days.
It grew to about 4 feet tall, compared with over 6 feet for our plants in the ground. It started producing about 2 months later than our in-ground okra, but once it got going it was prolific.

Extension guides don't list okra by name, but Texas A&M AgriLife says [5-gallon containers are the most suitable size](https://aggie-horticulture.tamu.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/10/2013/09/EHT-062.pdf) for fruiting crops like tomatoes, peppers and eggplant. Okra is a big plant, so treat 5 gallons as the minimum for one plant. A bigger container holds more water and needs it less often.

Whatever you use, it needs [holes in the bottom for drainage](https://hgic.clemson.edu/factsheet/container-vegetable-gardening/) so the roots never sit in water. A bucket with a few holes drilled in the bottom works well.

sections.title: The best soil for container okra

blocks.text: Use potting mix. Clemson Extension notes that [soil straight from the garden is usually too heavy](https://hgic.clemson.edu/factsheet/container-vegetable-gardening/) for a container, while packaged potting soil makes a good container medium.

Put the container in your sunniest spot. Vegetables grown for their fruit need [at least 5 hours of direct sun, and do better with 8 to 10](https://hgic.clemson.edu/factsheet/container-vegetable-gardening/).

Containers dry out much faster than garden beds. Clemson Extension suggests checking them [at least once a day, and twice on hot, dry or windy days](https://hgic.clemson.edu/factsheet/container-vegetable-gardening/). Water until it runs out of the drainage holes.

blocks.title: From Olivia's garden
blocks.text: Our family's bucket okra got water every 2 days in a North Texas summer. Feel the soil a couple of inches down, and water whenever it's dry.

If your potting mix has fertilizer in it, Clemson Extension says it should carry plants for [8 to 10 weeks](https://hgic.clemson.edu/factsheet/container-vegetable-gardening/). After that, use a water-soluble fertilizer at the label rate every 2 to 3 weeks, and never more than the label says.

The same timing as okra in the ground: plant once the soil is at least 65°F, about 2 to 3 weeks after your last frost. See [when to plant okra](/okra/when-to-plant-okra) for your hardiness zone. For growing tips that apply to every okra plant, see [how to grow okra](/okra/how-to-grow-okra).

faq.question: Can you grow okra in a pot?
faq.answer: Yes. Our family grew a prolific Clemson Spineless plant in a 5-gallon bucket with drainage holes and potting mix. Give it full sun and check the soil every day in summer.

faq.question: What size pot does okra need?
faq.answer: At least 5 gallons for one plant. Bigger is better, since a larger container holds more water and dries out more slowly.

faq.question: How tall does okra get in a container?
faq.answer: Shorter than in the ground. Our family's bucket okra reached about 4 feet, compared with over 6 feet for the same variety in our garden beds.

faq.question: Does container okra produce as much as okra in the ground?
faq.answer: In our experience it starts later, about 2 months behind our in-ground plants, but it was prolific once it got going.
